sources.title: Enfield withdraws from New Town process following change in leadership
sources.verified_claim: Enfield Council formally withdrew support for the New Town programme and shifted emphasis toward brownfield-first development and town-centre regeneration while retaining a stated commitment to homes and jobs.

sources.title: Joyce Avenue & Snell's Park Regeneration
sources.verified_claim: Enfield reports construction of the first new homes starting on 2 June 2026 and revised phasing that brings Block B forward within a programme of around 2,000 homes.

sources.title: Future schemes
sources.verified_claim: For Exeter Road Estate Phase 1, Enfield says a revised application received a resolution to grant on 17 March 2026, contractor tender evaluation was anticipated by July and construction restart is aimed for autumn 2026.

sources.title: New board to help protect Enfield’s heritage and shape future development
sources.verified_claim: Enfield approved a Conservation and Heritage Advisory Board to inform consideration of development affecting conservation areas, listed buildings, parks and green spaces.

sources.title: Planning approval secured for Waterloo and Queen Street Site in Romford
sources.verified_claim: Havering reports approval for Blocks 9 and 10 of the Waterloo and Queen Street regeneration in Romford, delivering more than 107 affordable homes plus community and landscaped public space.

sources.title: 100 Day plan for Havering restores stability to the Council
sources.verified_claim: Havering launched a 100-day plan on 22 July 2026 focused on stabilising governance and finances before setting a longer-term roadmap, with stated aims including homes for local people and a place attractive to live, work and invest.

sources.title: Lambeth: Shaping the borough's future
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth Council says the new Local Plan will guide sustainable and inclusive growth over the next 15 years, with first community work starting in September 2026 and adoption targeted for spring 2029.

sources.title: Oval and Kennington Development Area (OAKDA)
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth describes OAKDA as a potential major redevelopment covering the Oval gasworks and 16 surrounding parcels, with future applications potentially delivering over 1,400 jobs, 1,250 homes and improved open space, subject to planning and Local Plan changes.

sources.title: Weekly planning lists
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's official weekly planning list page shows current July 2026 validated application lists, including the week ending 17 July, providing a live planning-pipeline freshness signal without implying parcel applicability.
